title: Do hypotheses about what separates two sets of documents survive a held-out check?
summary: On 5,313 real GoEmotions comments, a word-counting proposer that picks the 20 words most associated with negative emotion in a small discovery sample overstates their effects 7.6× at 100 discovery comments (0.095 against 0.013 held-out) and 1.5× at 2,000. A Benjamini–Hochberg check on 3,000 held-out comments confirms 0.8 of the 20 at 100 comments and 14.7 at 2,000, and with shuffled labels confirms almost none (at most 5.5% of splits any), but 36–59% of confirmed hypotheses are the label's own vocabulary (“sorry”, “hate”), so replication is not explanation. The proposer is not an LLM, and the restatement flag is a crude word list.
